\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Noise --- Density: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian density bound under noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho,x,z\in\mathbb R$ and $v>0$ satisfy $v+\rho^2=1$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi
v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$. Then
\[p_v(\rho x,z)\le\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\sqrt{2\pi v}}\exp(x^2/2)\right)p_1(0,z).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Domination of a Gaussian product measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianNoise_le_smul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianNoise_le_smul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianReal_eq_withDensity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $x\in\bbr^n$. Let $v\ge0$ with
$v\ne0$, and suppose $v+\rho^2=1$. Then there is a finite nonnegative extended real
constant $C$ such that the product of the Gaussian measures with means $\rho x_i$ and
variance $v$ is dominated by $C$ times the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability under a Gaussian noise shift]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_integrand}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_integrand}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianAffine_pi, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianNoise_le_smul, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be
integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$, and fix any
$x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $y\mapsto f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)$ is integrable with
respect to $\gamma_n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian density identity under noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho,x,z\in\mathbb R$ and $v>0$ satisfy $v+\rho^2=1$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi
v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$. Then
\[p_v(\rho x,z)=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\sqrt{2\pi v}}\exp(x^2/2)\exp\left(-\frac{(\rho z-x)^2}{2v}\right)\right)p_1(0,z).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian exponent identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_exponent_sum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_exponent_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho,s\in\mathbb R$ with $s\ne0$, and let
$x,y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[\sum_{i=1}^n -\frac{(\rho y_i-x_i)^2}{2s^2}=-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{x_i}{s}-\frac{\rho y_i}{s}\right)^2.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian density under noise decomposition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_noise_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_noise_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_exponent_sum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_noise_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $\rho,s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $s\ne0$ and $s^2+\rho^2=1$.
For all $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$, the product of the Gaussian densities with means $\rho x_i$
and variance $s^2$, evaluated at $y_i$, equals
\[\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\sqrt{2\pi s^2}}\right)^n\exp\!\left(\frac{1}{2}\sum_i x_i^2\right)\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sum_i\left(\frac{x_i-\rho y_i}{s}\right)^2\right)\prod_i p_1(0,y_i),\]
where $p_1(0,y_i)$ is the standard Gaussian density at $y_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian noise integral factorization]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianNoise_densityFactorization}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianNoise_densityFactorization}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensity_noise_eq, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_pi_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianAffine_pi, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho,s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $s\ne0$ and
$s^2+\rho^2=1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$. With $Y$
distributed according to the product standard Gaussian measure, one has
\[\mathbb E\bigl[f(\rho x+sY)\bigr]=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\sqrt{2\pi s^2}}\right)^n e^{\|x\|^2/2}\,\mathbb E\left[f(Y)\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_i\left(\frac{x_i}{s}-\frac{\rho y_i}{s}\right)^2\right)\right],\]
where the expectation on the right is over $Y$.
\end{lemma}
